MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The step bits fit my recent rivet and rivet nut work because they would help me make different hole sizes in sheet metal and complement my existing drill set.",
    "The small self tapping screws fit my repair and assembly work, while the 1/4-20 machine screws could match my recent rivet nuts if the length is suitable.",
    "Disposable gloves make sense for messy workshop tasks, although I would check their chemical compatibility before using them with resin."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The printer filaments assume a printing project that my recent purchases do not establish; buying tools and resin does not mean I need printing supplies.",
    "The large lag screws serve a heavy timber fastening task I do not currently have, despite resembling the fasteners I buy.",
    "The disc magnets have no clear role in my current projects, and the second step bit overlaps with the broader set I would choose this time."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in making and repairing things seems to have been stretched into an assumed need for 3D printing materials.",
    "My repeated fastener purchases seem to have been treated as interest in any screws, even though dimensions, thread type, and intended use determine whether I can use them."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent rivets, rivet nuts, bolts, and cutting wheels suggest connected drilling and assembly tasks; supplies that support those tasks feel more relevant.",
    "Compatibility matters: matching threads, suitable screw lengths, and useful hole sizes are stronger reasons to choose something than a general workshop connection.",
    "I want tools that add useful capabilities to what I already own; two overlapping step bit options do not create two separate needs."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations partly understood my repair and fastening work but stretched that interest into unsupported printing needs and hardware without a clear current use."
}
